metadata.vulnerability_class: Improper Control of Generation of Code
attack_steps: Identify every feature that compiles or evaluates user-authored logic
Probe the expression context for accessible variables, functions, and object properties
Demonstrate evaluation of logic outside the tenant or role boundary
Confirm the compiled rule persists and executes on later business transactions

text: Attack pattern: A notification service builds an email or webhook body by concatenating a customer-supplied name. The name contains quotes and newlines that terminate the intended field and create additional headers or JSON members, so the recipient acts on an approval or payment instruction the sender never authorized. State transition: VALUE_ACCEPTED -> MESSAGE_ASSEMBLED -> ENCODING_OMITTED -> RECEIVER_REPARSES -> UNAUTHORIZED_ACTION. Variants include header injection, JSON member injection through unescaped quotes, XML entity confusion, and encoding applied to a truncated value. The attacker iterates until the business outcome, not merely an error message or response code, changes. Repeating the sequence across accounts or tenants turns a single-unit discrepancy into a systematic loss.

metadata.title: CWE-116 Exploitation Pattern: Structured Message Corruption Across Components
metadata.vulnerability_class: Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output
attack_steps: Find every place user data is embedded in JSON, XML, headers, or email bodies
Submit quotes, newlines, and entity syntax and inspect the receiver's parsed view
Check whether the receiver acts on injected members or headers
Confirm a business action such as an approval or settlement change

text: Attack pattern: A document or image import path reads a declared length from the uploaded file and returns the corresponding bytes in a preview or error response. By declaring a length larger than the payload, the attacker receives adjacent memory content that includes identifiers or tokens belonging to another request or tenant. State transition: MALFORMED_INPUT_UPLOADED -> LENGTH_TRUSTED -> READ_BEYOND_BUFFER -> ADJACENT_DATA_RETURNED -> CREDENTIAL_OR_TENANT_LEAK. Variants include negative offsets, truncated headers, and chunked encodings whose declared size exceeds the received body. The attacker iterates until the business outcome, not merely an error message or response code, changes. Repeating the sequence across accounts or tenants turns a single-unit discrepancy into a systematic loss.

metadata.title: CWE-125 Exploitation Pattern: Length-Trusted Read Disclosing Adjacent Records
attack_steps: Identify parsers that trust a length or offset field from the request
Submit truncated and oversized length declarations and inspect returned bytes
Check responses and error pages for data that belongs to another scope
Use any leaked identifier to attempt a cross-tenant or privileged action

text: Attack pattern: A cart endpoint accepts items[<index>][quantity] and items[<index>][price]. The attacker supplies a large or negative index, or an index that maps to another user's cart line after server-side sorting, and changes the quantity or price of an item they do not own. State transition: INDEX_SUBMITTED -> BOUNDS_CHECK_ABSENT -> WRONG_ELEMENT_SELECTED -> VALUE_MUTATED -> UNAUTHORIZED_BUSINESS_EFFECT. Variants include negative indices, sparse arrays, index reuse after filtering, and indices into merged multi-tenant collections. The attacker iterates until the business outcome, not merely an error message or response code, changes. Repeating the sequence across accounts or tenants turns a single-unit discrepancy into a systematic loss.

metadata.title: CWE-129 Exploitation Pattern: Positional Selection of Another Owner's Record
attack_steps: Find every array-shaped request parameter and the collection it addresses
Submit negative, zero, oversized, and sparse indices
Determine which element was actually read or written from persisted state
Confirm modification of an element outside the caller's ownership

text: Attack pattern: A bulk export computes buffer size as item_count * fixed_size but then serializes variable-length fields. With a crafted oversized field the write exceeds the allocation, corrupting adjacent data or truncating a settlement report so that entries are silently dropped. State transition: SIZE_COMPUTED -> ALLOCATION_UNDERSIZED -> WRITE_EXCEEDS_BOUNDS -> DATA_CORRUPTED_OR_TRUNCATED -> SETTLEMENT_ERROR. Variants include integer overflow in size multiplication, per-item overhead omitted, and encoded output larger than the source string. The attacker iterates until the business outcome, not merely an error message or response code, changes. Repeating the sequence across accounts or tenants turns a single-unit discrepancy into a systematic loss.

metadata.title: CWE-131 Exploitation Pattern: Undersized Allocation in Bulk Business Exports
attack_steps: Locate bulk, export, and batch paths that pre-compute allocation or quota
Submit variable-length and boundary-sized fields that change the real output size
Inspect output completeness and integrity for truncation or corruption
Confirm a business discrepancy such as dropped settlement lines

text: Attack pattern: An audit log records the user's display name by calling a formatting function with the name as the format argument. The attacker sets the name to a sequence of conversion specifiers and receives stack or heap content in the log viewer, including session identifiers or other tenants' data. State transition: VALUE_ACCEPTED -> USED_AS_FORMAT -> SPECIFIER_INTERPRETED -> MEMORY_DISCLOSED_OR_WRITTEN -> SESSION_OR_STATE_COMPROMISE. Variants include positional specifiers, width modifiers that amplify disclosure, and logging frameworks with printf-style message templates. The attacker iterates until the business outcome, not merely an error message or response code, changes. Repeating the sequence across accounts or tenants turns a single-unit discrepancy into a systematic loss.

metadata.title: CWE-134 Exploitation Pattern: Format Specifiers in Audit Logging
attack_steps: Find formatting and logging calls that receive user data
Submit conversion specifiers and observe output differences
Attempt to read stack values and correlate them with secrets
Assess whether write specifiers can alter control data

text: Attack pattern: An authorization check denies access to the resource path Admin but the storage layer resolves admin case-insensitively. The attacker requests Admin, passes the deny-list, and modifies the administrator's record. Variants use mixed-case email addresses to claim invitations or reuse coupons. State transition: IDENTIFIER_SUBMITTED -> CASE_CHECK_APPLIED -> LOOKUP_NORMALIZES -> PRIVILEGED_RECORD_RESOLVED -> UNAUTHORIZED_ACTION. Variants include mixed-case email invitations, case-variant coupon codes, and Unicode folding differences between services. The attacker iterates until the business outcome, not merely an error message or response code, changes. Repeating the sequence across accounts or tenants turns a single-unit discrepancy into a systematic loss.

metadata.title: CWE-178 Exploitation Pattern: Case Variant Passing Enforcement but Matching Privileged Data
attack_steps: Identify identifiers and roles that cross multiple services or storage layers
Submit case variants and compare authorization decisions with lookups
Test invitation, coupon, and share links with case mutations
Confirm access or benefit attached to the privileged record

text: Attack pattern: A redirect or file parameter is validated for a trusted prefix, then URL-decoded and normalized. The attacker submits an encoded traversal or an encoded second URL that becomes an external destination after decoding, and the business redirects users or reads a file outside the intended scope. State transition: RAW_VALUE_SUBMITTED -> CHECK_ON_RAW -> CANONICALIZATION_APPLIED -> RESTRICTED_VALUE_REVEALED -> RESTRICTION_BYPASSED. Variants include double URL encoding, Unicode normalization, dot-segment resolution, and case folding after the check. The attacker iterates until the business outcome, not merely an error message or response code, changes. Repeating the sequence across accounts or tenants turns a single-unit discrepancy into a systematic loss.

metadata.title: CWE-180 Exploitation Pattern: Encoded Value Changing Meaning After Validation
metadata.vulnerability_class: Incorrect Behavior Order: Validate Before Canonicalize
attack_steps: Identify parameters validated for path, host, or allowed-value constraints
Submit encoded, doubled-encoded, and normalized variants
Compare the checked form with the form used by the sink
Confirm the sink acts on the canonicalized restricted value

text: Attack pattern: An upload allow-list permits the generic image type plus SVG, and the SVG is served from the same origin with script execution. The attacker uploads a crafted SVG that performs actions as the victim, or a document type that the previewer executes with server privileges. State transition: INPUT_SUBMITTED -> ALLOWLIST_ACCEPTS -> UNINTENDED_CAPABILITY_PRESENT -> TRUSTED_CONTEXT_USED -> PRIVILEGE_OR_DATA_EFFECT. Variants include prefix-based host allow-lists, wildcard subdomain rules, and MIME allow-lists that trust the client-declared type. The attacker iterates until the business outcome, not merely an error message or response code, changes. Repeating the sequence across accounts or tenants turns a single-unit discrepancy into a systematic loss.

metadata.title: CWE-183 Exploitation Pattern: Overbroad Allow-List Granting Unintended Capability
attack_steps: Extract the effective allow-list from behavior and documentation
Submit values at the edge of the list, including nested and derived types
Determine what capability each permitted value carries in the trusted context
Confirm an action or data access beyond the feature's purpose

text: Attack pattern: A coupon or referral field blocks the literal string used in a known abuse report but accepts case variants, zero-width characters, or an equivalent field in the GraphQL mutation. The attacker applies the same promotion repeatedly and the fraud control never sees the blocked literal. State transition: BLOCKED_FORM_SUBMITTED -> DENYLIST_MATCHED -> VARIANT_SUBMITTED -> LIST_MISSES -> BUSINESS_ABUSE. Variants include case and Unicode variants, alternate parameters that reach the same sink, and encoding differences between JSON, form, and multipart bodies. The attacker iterates until the business outcome, not merely an error message or response code, changes. Repeating the sequence across accounts or tenants turns a single-unit discrepancy into a systematic loss.

metadata.title: CWE-184 Exploitation Pattern: Equivalent Forms Bypassing a Finite Deny-List
attack_steps: Enumerate the blocked forms from error messages and documentation
Generate equivalent representations and alternate parameters
Identify which representations reach the same business sink
Confirm the abuse outcome the deny-list was meant to prevent

text: Attack pattern: A wallet endpoint debits a fixed fee before validating that the balance covers it. The attacker submits a debit on a zero balance, the unsigned total wraps to the maximum value, and the account shows an enormous credit that can be spent or transferred. State transition: BALANCE_ZERO -> DEBIT_INITIATED -> SUBTRACTION_WRAPS -> HUGE_BALANCE -> TRANSFER_OR_PURCHASE. Variants include refund larger than the original charge, repeated reversal of a settled transaction, and negative quantity multiplied into an unsigned total. The attacker iterates until the business outcome, not merely an error message or response code, changes. Repeating the sequence across accounts or tenants turns a single-unit discrepancy into a systematic loss.

metadata.title: CWE-191 Exploitation Pattern: Debit Wraparound into a Spendlable Credit
attack_steps: Locate balance, stock, and counter updates that perform subtraction
Drive the value to its minimum and submit a larger debit or refund
Inspect the resulting stored value for wraparound
Attempt to spend or transfer the inflated balance

text: Attack pattern: A promotion allows one redemption per account, but the check reads the redemption count before the new row is inserted and compares with <=. The attacker redeems twice, then scripts the same pattern across accounts to accumulate discounts beyond the intended budget. State transition: LIMIT_DEFINED -> COUNT_CHECKED -> COMPARISON_OFF_BY_ONE -> EXTRA_UNIT_ACCEPTED -> LIMIT_EXCEEDED. Variants include concurrent redemption of the last unit, per-batch limits, and quantity caps evaluated before merging duplicate line items. The attacker iterates until the business outcome, not merely an error message or response code, changes. Repeating the sequence across accounts or tenants turns a single-unit discrepancy into a systematic loss.

metadata.title: CWE-193 Exploitation Pattern: One Extra Unit Beyond a Business Limit
attack_steps: Identify every per-user, per-order, and per-coupon limit
Drive the counter to the boundary and submit one extra operation
Test duplicate line items and concurrent requests at the boundary
Confirm the surplus unit is persisted and usable

text: Attack pattern: A payment service validates the amount as a 64-bit decimal but stores it in a 32-bit integer of minor units. The attacker submits an amount just above the 32-bit range, the stored value truncates to a small positive number, and the payment is accepted for far less than authorized. State transition: AMOUNT_SUBMITTED -> VALIDATED_AT_HIGH_PRECISION -> CAST_TO_SMALLER_TYPE -> VALUE_TRUNCATED -> UNDERPAYMENT_OR_OVERCREDIT. Variants include decimal-to-integer truncation of fractions, 64-bit to 32-bit narrowing, and precision loss in currency conversion. The attacker iterates until the business outcome, not merely an error message or response code, changes. Repeating the sequence across accounts or tenants turns a single-unit discrepancy into a systematic loss.

metadata.title: CWE-197 Exploitation Pattern: Amount Truncation Between Validation and Settlement
attack_steps: Identify amount, quantity, and identifier fields with mixed precision across services
Submit values just above and below type boundaries and fractional values
Compare the validated amount with the persisted and settled amount
Confirm a monetary difference that favors the attacker

text: Attack pattern: A coupon validation endpoint returns 200 with a discount for a valid code and 404 for an invalid one, while unauthenticated callers can enumerate the whole code space. The attacker harvests every active promotion, then combines them with a redemption flaw to obtain repeated discounts. State transition: CANDIDATE_SUBMITTED -> DISTINCT_BRANCH_RETURNED -> STATE_INFERRED -> RESOURCE_ENUMERATED -> SECONDARY_ABUSE. Variants include timing differences, header-length differences, and localized messages that reveal existence while claiming to be generic. The attacker iterates until the business outcome, not merely an error message or response code, changes. Repeating the sequence across accounts or tenants turns a single-unit discrepancy into a systematic loss.

metadata.title: CWE-204 Exploitation Pattern: Identifier Harvesting Through Response Differences
attack_steps: Collect responses for known-valid, known-invalid, and nonexistent resources
Compare status, body, headers, and timing across the three sets
Automate enumeration of the candidate space at a safe rate
Use the harvested identifiers in a follow-on business abuse

text: Attack pattern: An order confirmation endpoint returns the generated verification code in the error body when the submitted code is wrong, framed as debugging context. The attacker submits any value, reads the correct code from the error, and completes the order or verification step. State transition: INVALID_INPUT_SUBMITTED -> ERROR_PATH_TAKEN -> SENSITIVE_CONTEXT_RENDERED -> SECRET_EXTRACTED -> WORKFLOW_COMPLETED. Variants include stack traces, SQL error detail, template paths, and validation errors that echo the expected token. The attacker iterates until the business outcome, not merely an error message or response code, changes. Repeating the sequence across accounts or tenants turns a single-unit discrepancy into a systematic loss.

metadata.title: CWE-209 Exploitation Pattern: Verification Code Leaked Through a Validation Error
metadata.vulnerability_class: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information
attack_steps: Drive every input validation and workflow endpoint into its error branches
Inspect responses for tokens, identifiers, paths, and internal state
Correlate disclosed values with the next required step
Complete the workflow using the leaked value

text: Attack pattern: A legacy support export includes the user table with a plaintext password column. An analyst with report access downloads the export, authenticates as an administrator, and approves payments or changes settlement accounts without triggering credential-reset controls. State transition: CREDENTIAL_STORED_RECOVERABLE -> STORE_READ -> PASSWORD_RECOVERED -> AUTHENTICATION_AS_VICTIM -> PRIVILEGED_BUSINESS_ACTION. Variants include encrypted-but-decryptable columns, passwords in application logs, and credential material in backup or analytics exports. The attacker iterates until the business outcome, not merely an error message or response code, changes. Repeating the sequence across accounts or tenants turns a single-unit discrepancy into a systematic loss.

metadata.title: CWE-256 Exploitation Pattern: Support Export Enabling Account Takeover
attack_steps: Inspect storage schemas, exports, and logs reachable with low privilege
Determine whether passwords are hashed with a password-specific function
Recover a test account's password from the reachable artifact
Authenticate and confirm access to privileged business functions

text: Attack pattern: A deployment image contains a support account password used to bypass normal approval for refunds. The attacker extracts it from a public container image, authenticates to the support interface, and issues refunds or credits without the four-eyes review the business relies on. State transition: ARTIFACT_OBTAINED -> CREDENTIAL_EXTRACTED -> SHARED_SECRET_USED -> SUPPORT_ACCESS_GRANTED -> PRIVILEGED_ACTION. Variants include default passwords, credentials in mobile binaries, and shared secrets reused across environments. The attacker iterates until the business outcome, not merely an error message or response code, changes. Repeating the sequence across accounts or tenants turns a single-unit discrepancy into a systematic loss.

metadata.title: CWE-259 Exploitation Pattern: Embedded Support Password in a Deployment Artifact
attack_steps: Collect public artifacts, images, and configuration reachable by the attacker
Extract candidate credentials and identify the accounts they protect
Authenticate and enumerate the privileges of the account
Demonstrate a business action unavailable to a normal user

text: Attack pattern: When a team invitation is accepted, the invitation's creator role is copied to the invitee instead of the role specified in the invite. The server returns a total of 9.9 instead of 99. The attacker repeats the value in the order-placement request so the two calculations agree, then pays the reduced amount. State transition: DISH_SELECTED -> CART_CALCULATED -> QUANTITY_DECIMALIZED -> TOTAL_REDUCED -> ORDER_PLACED -> DELIVERED. Variants include 0.02 for an even smaller charge, mixed lines where one quantity is fractional, and negative quantities that invert the line total.

metadata.title: Decimal Quantity in the Cart and Payment Requests Paying a Fraction of the Price
metadata.report_title: [www.zomato.com] Tampering with Order Quantity and paying less amount then actual amount, leads to business loss
metadata.state_transition: DISH_SELECTED -> CART_CALCULATED -> QUANTITY_DECIMALIZED -> TOTAL_REDUCED -> ORDER_PLACED -> DELIVERED
attack_steps: Add a dish and capture the cart-calculation and order-placement requests
Change the quantity to a decimal below one in both requests
Confirm the recalculated total and proceed to payment
Verify the order is accepted and fulfilled at the reduced amount

text: Attack pattern: rewrite the seat descriptor in a multipart request. The attacker selects a season ticket and three seats, intercepts the add-tickets request, and replaces 3-seats-3 with 10-seats-10. The order summary shows a zero-dollar total, and the order can be completed for any number of seats. State transition: TICKET_SELECTED -> SEATS_CHOSEN -> MULTIPART_FIELD_TAMPERED -> ZERO_TOTAL_RENDERED -> ORDER_COMPLETED. Variants include negative seat counts, price suffixes inconsistent with the count, and replaying the same field across different add-on identifiers.

metadata.title: Multipart Add-On Seat Field Raised to Ten Seats for a Zero-Dollar Order
metadata.report_title: attacker can book unlimited tickets in free at https://aaf.com/checkout/order-received/21237/?key=wc_order_5bbef48fa35b2
attack_steps: Select a paid ticket and capture the add-tickets multipart request
Rewrite the seat descriptor to a higher count while keeping the price component low
Confirm the order summary total and the seat count
Complete the order and verify the tickets are issued

text: Attack pattern: observe the issuance response instead of the SMS. The attacker opens the subscription management page, enters a victim's number, and inspects the network response for the send-otp call. The response contains the OTP value. The attacker submits it and proceeds to modify the subscription. State transition: NUMBER_SUBMITTED -> OTP_ISSUED -> RESPONSE_INSPECTED -> OTP_EXTRACTED -> OTP_SUBMITTED -> SUBSCRIPTION_CHANGED. Variants include predictable OTPs derived from the number, OTP reuse across numbers, and the same endpoint being reused by other features.

metadata.title: Reading otpKey from the Response and Managing Another Subscriber's Plan
metadata.report_title: OTP bypass - Unintended disclosure of OTP to client allows attacker to manage users' subscriptions
metadata.state_transition: NUMBER_SUBMITTED -> OTP_ISSUED -> RESPONSE_INSPECTED -> OTP_EXTRACTED -> OTP_SUBMITTED -> SUBSCRIPTION_CHANGED
attack_steps: Open the subscription flow and capture the send-otp request
Inspect the response body and headers for the OTP value
Submit the extracted value to the verification prompt
Change the subscriber's plan and confirm the persisted state

text: Attack pattern: exploit the gap between plan selection and settlement. The attacker starts a paid plan with an empty card, observes the failure, raises the seat count to trigger a second failure, then cancels. The account remains on the paid tier and every paid feature stays usable. State transition: PLAN_SELECTED -> PAYMENT_FAILS -> SEATS_INCREASED -> PAYMENT_FAILS_AGAIN -> SUBSCRIPTION_CANCELLED -> PAID_FEATURES_ACTIVE. Variants include downgrade after upgrade, trial-to-paid transitions without settlement, and seat changes that re-trigger pricing without re-checking the invoice.

metadata.title: Failing Payment, Inflating Seats, then Cancelling to Keep the Paid Plan
metadata.report_title: [app.lemlist.com] Improper handling of payment lead to bypass payment
metadata.state_transition: PLAN_SELECTED -> PAYMENT_FAILS -> SEATS_INCREASED -> PAYMENT_FAILS_AGAIN -> SUBSCRIPTION_CANCELLED -> PAID_FEATURES_ACTIVE
attack_steps: Start a paid plan with a payment method that will fail
Confirm the failure notification and the plan state
Increase seats to trigger a second failed charge
Cancel the subscription and confirm paid features remain available

text: Attack pattern: replay an idempotent-looking acceptance operation. The attacker receives a fee-discount offer, captures the accept request, and repeats it. Each response reports success and each repetition adds the full discount to the fee-free balance. A race is not even required. State transition: OFFER_ISSUED -> ACCEPT_REQUEST_CAPTURED -> REQUEST_REPLAYED -> CREDIT_APPLIED_EACH_TIME -> BALANCE_EXCEEDS_OFFER. Variants include concurrent acceptance to bypass a check-then-act gap, and reuse of the offer identifier across accounts.

metadata.title: Repeating accept_fee_discount_offer to Stack Unlimited Fee-Free Processing
metadata.report_title: Fee discounts can be redeemed many times, resulting in unlimited fee-free transactions
attack_steps: Capture the request that accepts the fee-discount offer
Replay it sequentially and observe the applied-credit balance
Repeat concurrently to test for a check-then-act race
Confirm total applied credit exceeds the offer value

text: Attack pattern: reuse a public code as a permanent entitlement. The attacker applies the free-shipping coupon, observes the total drop by the shipping fee, completes the order, and repeats on the next order. Because no redemption is recorded, nothing distinguishes the first use from the hundredth. State transition: CART_BUILT -> COUPON_APPLIED -> SHIPPING_ZEROED -> ORDER_PLACED -> COUPON_APPLIED_AGAIN. Variants include applying the code alongside another discount, reusing it across accounts, and automating order creation to maximize the waived fees.

metadata.title: Reapplying a Disclosed Promo Code to Every Order for Zero Shipping
metadata.report_title: Unlimited Reuse of Coupon Code Allows Free Shipping on All Orders on a Merch Store
attack_steps: Collect active promotional codes from public reports and marketing pages
Apply the code and confirm the shipping charge is removed
Place the order and apply the same code to a second order
Verify no redemption record or usage limit blocks reuse

text: Attack pattern: write the post-approval state directly instead of earning it. The attacker creates a campaign and an ad, observes that the dashboard shows PENDING, then issues a PATCH to the ad endpoint with admin_approval APPROVED and effective_status ACTIVE. The ad becomes deliverable and a confirmation email is sent. State transition: CAMPAIGN_CREATED -> AD_PENDING -> PATCH_STATE_FIELDS -> APPROVED_ACTIVE -> AD_DELIVERED_WITHOUT_PAYMENT. Variants include writing only effective_status, toggling configured_status after creation, and using a bulk or legacy endpoint that shares the same model.

metadata.title: PATCH Setting admin_approval to APPROVED and effective_status to ACTIVE
metadata.report_title: Able to approve admin approval and change effective status without adding payment details.
attack_steps: Create a campaign and an ad and note the PENDING status
Capture the ad update request and its writable fields
PATCH admin_approval and effective_status to approved and active
Confirm delivery and the approval notification without payment

text: Attack pattern: claim the identity that was invited. A member views the pending owner invitation list, learns the victim's email, registers a new account with that address without verifying it, and accepts the invitation. The platform promotes the new account to owner. State transition: INVITATION_SENT -> MEMBER_READS_RECIPIENT -> UNVERIFIED_ACCOUNT_CREATED -> INVITATION_ACCEPTED -> OWNER_ROLE_GRANTED. Variants include case or plus-address variants of the email and acceptance from an existing account whose address was changed to the invited one.

metadata.title: Registering the Invited Owner's Email and Accepting the Invitation
metadata.report_title: Shopify Partners Invitation Process Allows Privilege Escalation Without Email Verification
attack_steps: Obtain a partner account and view pending invitations as a low-privilege member
Register an account using the invited owner's email without verifying it
Accept the invitation from the new account
Confirm owner-level access to the partner account

text: Attack pattern: reserve seats before the cap applies. The administrator on the free tier invites a large batch of users while the active member count is within the limit, then each invitee signs up and joins successfully. Inviting more afterwards is blocked, but the pre-issued invitations still convert. State transition: PLAN_CAP_3 -> MASS_INVITES_ISSUED -> CAP_REACHED -> INVITEES_ACCEPT -> MEMBER_COUNT_EXCEEDS_CAP. Variants include concurrent acceptance at the boundary and invitations issued by multiple admins.

metadata.title: Mass Invitations Accepted After the Workspace Reaches Its Plan Limit
metadata.report_title: User Limit Bypass via Pending Invitations in Workspace System
attack_steps: Create a workspace on the lowest plan tier and note the seat cap
Issue invitations to many addresses while under the cap
Sign up as one invitee and confirm acceptance at the cap
Repeat for the remaining invitees and confirm the member count exceeds the plan

text: Attack pattern: change the flag that the UI uses to gate the action. The attacker opens the team section, attempts an invitation, and sees the request blocked with a 2FA prompt. A match-and-replace rule flips the returned flag from false to true, the page refreshes, and the invitation is sent successfully with 2FA still disabled. State transition: INVITE_ATTEMPTED -> CLIENT_BLOCKS -> FLAG_TAMPERED -> INVITE_REQUEST_SENT -> INVITATION_CREATED. Variants include replaying the invite request directly without the UI and deleting the flag field so the server defaults to allowed.

metadata.title: Match-and-Replace Flipping the 2FA Flag to Send Invitations
metadata.report_title: 2FA requirement bypass when inviting team members
attack_steps: Attempt an invitation with 2FA disabled and capture the blocked request
Identify the client flag or response field that gates the action
Flip the flag with match-and-replace or replay the request directly
Confirm the invitation is created while 2FA remains disabled

text: Attack pattern: remove the token that binds the decision to the reviewed version. The requester submits a file for approval, the approver reviews it and clicks approve, and the requester modifies the file before the request is forwarded. The approver removes the etag field from the JSON body and forwards; the backend records the approval against the new version. State transition: FILE_SUBMITTED -> REVIEWED -> MODIFIED -> ETAG_OMITTED -> APPROVAL_RECORDED -> UNREVIEWED_VERSION_APPROVED. Variants include an empty etag, a null value, and a stale etag from a different file.

metadata.title: Modify After Review then Approve With the ETag Field Removed
metadata.report_title: Approval app's file-freshness check can be bypassed by omitting the etag parameter, allowing approval of unreviewed file changes
metadata.state_transition: FILE_SUBMITTED -> REVIEWED -> MODIFIED -> ETAG_OMITTED -> APPROVAL_RECORDED -> UNREVIEWED_VERSION_APPROVED
attack_steps: Create an approval workflow and submit a file for review
Have the approver open and review the file
Modify the file before the approval request is sent
Remove the etag field from the approval body and forward it

text: Attack pattern: obtain a valid payment event for a cheap order and redirect its effect. The attacker registers for a low-cost ticket, pays, and captures the notification. They replay it with the ticket token of a different, expensive draft order, either by editing the query string with a valid body MAC or by sending an invalid MAC and relying on the fail-open branch. The expensive order is marked pending or completed and the ticket is published. State transition: CHEAP_PAYMENT_COMPLETED -> NOTIFICATION_CAPTURED -> TOKEN_SUBSTITUTED -> MAC_INVALID_OR_VALID -> EXPENSIVE_ORDER_CREDITED -> TICKET_PUBLISHED. Variants include reusing one notification across many orders and using the return path without any gateway call.

metadata.title: Invalid MAC and Reused Payment Token Marking Tickets Paid
metadata.report_title: Instamojo CampTix: fail-open MAC + webhook Credit without binding payment to order
attack_steps: Complete a low-value order and capture the gateway notification
Record the ticket token and the signed body fields
Replay with another order's token using an invalid MAC and then a valid body MAC
Confirm the target order is marked paid and the ticket published

text: Attack pattern: remove the state that the gate depends on. The attacker logs in with a stolen or guessed password, reaches the OTP page, deletes bb_refresh in the browser's cookie store, and refreshes. The application renders the authenticated area without an OTP submission. State transition: PASSWORD_ACCEPTED -> OTP_PAGE_SHOWN -> REFRESH_COOKIE_DELETED -> PAGE_REFRESHED -> AUTHENTICATED_ACCESS. Variants include clearing all cookies except the session cookie, replaying the post-login request without the refresh cookie, and editing the cookie value to an empty string.

metadata.title: Password Login then Cookie Deletion Landing in the Authenticated Session
metadata.report_title: Email OTP/2FA Bypass
attack_steps: Log in with a valid password to reach the OTP page
Inspect the cookies issued at that stage
Delete the refresh cookie and refresh or replay the request
Confirm access to authenticated functionality without the OTP

text: Attack pattern: stay under the rounding threshold. The program manager awards one cent repeatedly, each time with a computed fee of 0.002 that rounds to zero. Across many awards the recipient receives the full sum while the platform collects almost nothing. State transition: AWARD_SET -> FEE_COMPUTED -> FEE_ROUNDED_TO_ZERO -> AWARD_PAID -> FEE_EVADED. Variants include two-cent awards at the 0.004 boundary, mixed denominations, and bulk award endpoints that apply the same rounding per report.

metadata.title: Splitting a Reward into Cent-Sized Bounties to Avoid the Platform Fee
metadata.report_title: Rounding errors on rewarding a bounty leads to bypassing the 20% H1 commission fee
attack_steps: Determine the fee formula and the smallest award accepted
Submit awards at values whose fee rounds to zero
Repeat through the bulk endpoint and observe the billing ledger
Compare total fees with the expected percentage of total awards
